chunks: And when it is said: 'We are capable of mentioning the aspects of the ambiguous verses, but you are unable to mention a valid reason for the occultation,' we say: Our discourse is directed at the one who says 'I do not need to know the detailed aspects of the ambiguous verses, but that a general understanding suffices for me.' If you undertake that, it is out of your own volition. And if you are satisfied with that for yourselves, then we too are capable of mentioning the validity of the occultation and a wise purpose that does not contradict his infallibility. We will mention that later, and we have discussed it comprehensively in the book of Imamate.
ai.seo_question: What is the theological justification for the Imam's occultation in Shia thought?
ai.summary: Al-Tusi refutes the objection by distinguishing between those who require detailed exegesis of ambiguous verses and those satisfied with general knowledge, arguing that the latter can similarly accept the occultation's validity. He asserts that the hidden Imam's occultation possesses a wise purpose consistent with his infallibility, a topic he elaborates on in his seminal work, *Kitab al-Irghab*. This response underscores the Shia theological stance that divine wisdom in the Imam's absence does not negate his spiritual perfection or authority.
